title: Stamp 3: The Rise of the AfD
welcome_lead: Stamp the political backlash against immigration: the AfD.
meta_desc: A-Level German adventure on the AfD, populism, and integration debates.

concepts.def: Alternative fur Deutschland; right-wing populist party founded 2013, anti-immigration.
Patriotische Europaer gegen die Islamisierung des Abendlandes; Dresden-based protest movement from 2014.
Guiding culture; debated concept asserting German cultural norms for newcomers.
Integration Law of 2016 requiring courses and accelerating labour market access.
Dual citizenship; long restricted, increasingly permitted from 2024.
Parallel society; controversial term used to describe perceived ethnic enclaves.

walkthroughs.body_html: Originally founded in 2013 as a Eurosceptic party, the AfD shifted sharply rightward after 2015, capitalising on anti-immigration sentiment. It entered the Bundestag in 2017 with 12.6% of the vote.
The AfD performs especially strongly in eastern states such as Saxony and Thuringia. Federal intelligence agency BfV monitors parts of the party for extremism.

The 2016 Integrationsgesetz introduced compulsory integration and German language courses (Integrationskurse) while easing labour market access. Citizenship reform 2024 allows dual nationality and a path to citizenship after 5 years (3 with exceptional integration).
